To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

18F-FDGPET is a useful tool in the management of patients with well-differentiated carcinomas of the thyroid, especially in the follow-up and in patients with negative 123-iodide scan and high serum thyroglobulins.
18F-FDGPET is useful in the diagnosis and staging of thyroid malignancies.
18F-FGD PET is a useful tool for the diagnosis of thyroid malignancy, and for the assessment of the prognosis in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PET in the diagnosis of thyroid malignancies, with special emphasis to the role of PET-CT.
the potential role of 18FDG PET in the management of patients with thyroid cancer.
the role of 19F-FDG PET as a diagnostic imaging modality in thyroid cancer, especially in the follow-up.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
18F-FDGPET should be used as an adjunct to the standard imaging techniques in thyroid cancer patients.

18F-FFDG PET is a useful method in the follow-up in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer, in the assessment of the extent of the disease and in the differential diagnosis between benign and malignant thyroid nodules.

18F-FFDG PET is not yet a standard procedure for thyroid cancer, but is a useful and complementary diagnostic method in selected cases. (orig.) Titolo: Review. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET in the management of differentiated thyroid cancer: current status and perspectives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
18F-FD PET is a useful tool in the management of patients with thyroid cancer.

18F-FDg PET is a useful tool for the management of differentiated thyroid cancer patients with negative iodine scan and elevated thyroglobulin level, but it is still under investigation for other indications.
18F-FDGPET can be used to detect malignancy in patients with thyroid nodules and to detect recurrent thyroid cancer in patients with elevated serum Tg and negative radioiodine imaging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
18F-FD PET is an emerging technique for the diagnosis of thyroid malignancies and its clinical role should be further investigated.
PET is a useful tool in the management of well-differentiated tumours of the thyroid.

18F-FDGPET can be used to assess thyroid nodules with high uptake of 18F- FDG, to detect metastatic disease in thyroid carcinoma patients with elevated serum Tg levels and negative iodide scans and to detect residual or metastatic disease in differentiated thyroid cancer patients with negative iodine scans and positive Tg levels.
